title: Needle entry on the patient
view: The open mouth of a seated patient seen from the front, as the operator faces them: head at the top, the patient's right on the image left. Block on the right.
teachingPoint: Barrel over the opposite lower premolars; entry midway between the coronoid notch and the pterygomandibular raphe, about 1 cm above the lower molars' biting surfaces.
claims: Open mouth from the front, patient's right on the image left (house laterality; the record names no side).
Purple ring: the coronoid notch, felt through the cheek (record, steps 2).
Pale fold: the pterygomandibular raphe, medial to the notch (record, steps 3).
Red dot: entry at the midpoint between notch and raphe, 1 cm above the lower molars' occlusal plane (record, steps 5).
Syringe barrel over the patient's left lower premolars (record, steps 4); the needle is foreshortened because it runs back into the mouth.
Two labels: Coronoid notch, Pterygomandibular raphe.

geometry.why: entry is medial to the notch (on the patient's right, medial is right)
entry is lateral to the raphe
entry is above the lower molars' occlusal plane
entry is on the mucosa inside the mouth
syringe comes from the opposite side
barrel rests over the opposite premolars
notch and raphe are distinct landmarks either side of the entry
